text.text: Hulhumalé, an illustration by the Hulhumalé group, drawn over the HDC land use plan.
Hulhumalé is a reclaimed island in North Malé Atoll, just north of the airport island, Hulhulé.
The Sinamalé Bridge and a road across the airport link it to Malé, and public ferries run between the two.
Reclamation began in 1997. The island was planned from the start, to ease crowding and the housing shortage in Malé.
Hulhumalé was planned and built from nothing, and it is still growing.
island aerial or figure-ground map, with north arrow and scale bar
It takes in people from Malé and the outer atolls. It offers homes, shops, light industry, schools, hospitals and guesthouses.
The three islands share the work. Malé is the dense old capital and the seat of government. Hulhulé holds the airport. Hulhumalé is the planned extension, for homes, business and green space.
